```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(PGViS)
set.seed(1)
```

The final step turns per-variant metrics into one number per patient: the
PGViS score. This vignette runs end to end on the fixture.

The score has four steps. For a dataset with variant list $U$ and a sample $i$
carrying the variants $C_i$:

$$p_{fv} = \frac{\#\{u \in U : x_{fu} \le x_{fv}\}}{|U|}, \quad f \in \{|\Delta Wi|, \mathrm{LOR}\} \tag{1}$$
$$s_v = \left(p_{|\Delta Wi|,v}\, p_{\mathrm{LOR},v}\right)^{1/2} \tag{2}$$
$$S_i = \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{|C_i|}\textstyle\sum_{v \in C_i} s_v^{2}} \tag{3}$$
$$\mathrm{PGViS}_i = (S_i - \mathrm{mean}_{\mathrm{ref}}) / \mathrm{SD}_{\mathrm{ref}} \tag{4}$$

ΔAF is not used. It is the criterion that *selects* variants, so scoring on it
again makes the tumour-versus-reference comparison circular.

## From variants to samples

A variant is carried by some set of samples. To score samples, we first expand
each variant into one row per carrier.

```{r explode}
metrics <- pgvis_variant_metrics(pgvis_example("variants"),
                                 pgvis_example("predictions"))
metrics <- pgvis_filter_disruptive(metrics, ref_prob_min = 0.5,
                                   alt_prob_max = 0.5, min_carrier_frac = 0)

long <- pgvis_explode_carriers(metrics)
nrow(metrics)
nrow(long)          # one row per (variant, carrier)
```

Attach ancestry (needed for the standardisation, explained below):

```{r ancestry}
clin <- pgvis_example("clinical")
clin$superpopulation <- pgvis_map_superpopulation(clin$race)
long <- dplyr::left_join(long, clin[, c("sample", "superpopulation")],
                         by = "sample")
long <- long[!is.na(long$superpopulation), ]
```

Self-reported race maps to a 1000 Genomes superpopulation; anything that
doesn't map becomes `NA` and those samples are excluded rather than pooled
into a default group. Where you have genotype-inferred ancestry, prefer it.

## A reference arm

The score is defined relative to a reference cohort — typically the
1000 Genomes panel, run through the identical pipeline. The reference has its
own variant list, so its variants are ranked among themselves, exactly as the
cohort's are. Here we synthesise a reference arm so the vignette can score end
to end:

```{r panel}
ped <- pgvis_load_pedigree(
  system.file("extdata", "toy_pedigree.txt", package = "PGViS"))

ref_vars <- data.frame(
  var_site = sprintf("chrR:%d-%d(A>G)", 1000L * (1:60), 1000L * (1:60) + 1L),
  delta_wi_int = rnorm(60), log_odds_ratio = rnorm(60))
panel_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ped)), function(i) {
  v <- ref_vars[sample(60, 10), ]
  v$sample <- ped$sample[i]; v$superpopulation <- ped$superpopulation[i]
  v$cohort <- "1000Genomes"; v
}))
panel_long <- panel_long[!is.na(panel_long$superpopulation), ]

stacked <- dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::as_tibble(long), dplyr::as_tibble(panel_long))
```

## Variant scores and sample scores (Eq. 1–3)

```{r variant-score}
stacked <- pgvis_variant_score(stacked)
head(stacked[, c("cohort", "var_site", "p_delta_wi_int",
                 "p_log_odds_ratio", "variant_score")])
```

Each feature is ranked within the variant list of its **own** cohort
(`universe_col = "cohort"`), so features in different units are comparable and
the score does not depend on how long a cohort's list is. The two ranks are
combined by their geometric mean. A sample's raw score is then the root mean
square over the variants it carries:

```{r sample-score}
per_sample <- pgvis_sample_scores(stacked)
head(per_sample)
```

The root mean square stays on the same 0–1 scale however many variants a
person carries, so it does not simply grow with variant burden. A cumulative
sum would: it follows the length of each cohort's variant list.

## Standardising against the reference (Eq. 4)

```{r score}
scored <- pgvis_score(per_sample, reference_group = "1000Genomes")
head(scored[, c("sample", "cohort", "superpopulation", "pgvis_raw", "pgvis")])
```

The mean and standard deviation come from the reference samples of the *same
superpopulation*:

```{r reference}
attr(scored, "reference")
```

`pgvis_bind_panel()` is available when the cohort and reference have been
scored separately; it refuses to proceed if they share no superpopulation —
which would otherwise produce a table of all-`NA` z-scores instead of an error.

### Why ancestry matching is not optional

Allele-frequency divergence from a reference panel scales with how genetically
distant a sample is from that panel, and reference scores differ by about one
standard deviation across superpopulations. Standardise against the whole panel
and the score largely reports ancestry. Standardising *within* superpopulation
removes that confound. `pgvis_score(strata = NULL)` exists for a genuinely
homogeneous cohort and is the wrong choice otherwise.

### Freeze the reference for validation

The reference mean and SD are refit from the reference samples in front of you,
so two runs aren't on the same scale unless you say so. When you score a
validation cohort, reuse the discovery reference:

```{r frozen}
ref <- attr(scored, "reference")
s2  <- pgvis_score(per_sample, reference = ref)   # same scale as `scored`
all.equal(s2$pgvis, scored$pgvis)
```

### The previous composite

Versions before 0.2.0 averaged raw metrics per sample, standardised them with
the median and MAD of the reference and combined them with PC1-derived
weights. It is kept as `pgvis_score(df, method = "pca")` for reproducing
earlier results, but it includes ΔAF and follows list size, and its scores
are not on the same scale as the default.

## Comparing groups

`pgvis_compare_groups()` gives ROC AUC, Cohen's d and a permutation p-value —
and withholds them when a group is too small to interpret.

```{r compare}
demo <- data.frame(pgvis = c(rnorm(120, 0), rnorm(120, 1.1)),
                   group = rep(c("control", "case"), each = 120))
pgvis_compare_groups(demo, min_n = 50, n_perm = 500)[,
  c("n1", "n2", "auc", "cohens_d", "perm_p")]
```

Below `min_n` per group it returns `valid = FALSE` and a label saying so,
rather than a confident effect size from a dozen samples. The permutation
p-value uses the add-one estimator, so it's never reported as exactly zero.

## Survival

Downstream, but common enough to wrap. It runs a log-rank test across score
groups and a Cox model on the continuous score, supports covariates so you can
check the score isn't just reporting stage, and refuses non-binary event
coding.

```{r survival}
n <- 300
score <- rnorm(n)
time  <- rexp(n, rate = exp(0.7 * score) / 500)   # higher score, shorter time
sc  <- data.frame(sample = paste0("S", 1:n), pgvis = score)
cl  <- data.frame(sample = paste0("S", 1:n), time = time,
                  event = rbinom(n, 1, 0.8))

res <- pgvis_survival(sc, cl)
res$summary
```

`pgvis_plot_survival(res)` draws the Kaplan-Meier curves (with a risk table if
`survminer` is installed, base graphics otherwise).

## Provenance

`pgvis_run()` — the one-call wrapper for this whole R-side sequence — writes a
manifest next to the results recording the thresholds, the scoring method, the
reference mean and SD per stratum, input row counts and any QC warnings. Months later, when you need to know
exactly which settings produced a given table, the answer is sitting next to
it rather than lost to memory.

```{r run, eval = FALSE}
res <- pgvis_run(cfg, variants, clinical = clin,
                 reference_group = "1000Genomes")
```

## What can go wrong

- **Reference group absent.** The score is defined relative to a reference; if
  `reference_group` isn't in the data, `pgvis_score()` stops rather than
  standardising against nothing.
- **Too few reference samples in a stratum.** With fewer than two reference
  samples, or constant scores, the reference SD is undefined; those samples
  score as `NA` (with a message) rather than being given an invented scale.
- **Comparing scores across runs.** Only valid if the reference is frozen
  (`reference = attr(scored, "reference")`). Two independently-fit runs are
  not on the same scale.
- **Different variant lists.** Percentiles are taken within each cohort's own
  list, so the score says which variants of the list a person carries
  (high-ranking or low-ranking), not how large the raw features are. Tumour and
  reference lists are built separately and may overlap little, so the score
  gives moderate separation and is not a diagnostic.
- **Putting ΔAF back.** `pgvis_variant_score(features = c(..., "delta_af_alt"))`
  works but is circular: ΔAF selects the variants, and the function says so.

That's the whole pipeline. The [overview](PGViS.html) has the condensed
version, and [the cluster guide](pipeline.html) has the shell side in one
place.
